summary: Redwood AE + SE ran a Console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Aurora Tech is evaluating a pilot to replace parts of their inference stack; key concerns were token-level cost transparency, per-route SLOs, security (SOC 2/KMS/SSO), and quantization impact on quality. Agreement to run a short benchmark pilot and share usage exports; Redwood to provide tailored pricing and a benchmark plan.
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Grant: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sophie from Redwood, AE. Marco from our SE team is with me. Quick quick intros?
[00:08] Priya Shah: Hi, Priya, Head of MLOps at Aurora, we've got Daniel in platform and Marta from finance.
[00:15] Marco Diaz: Morning! We'll walk through the Console — especially the usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns, and then Q+A.
[00:24] Daniel Kim: Great, main thing for us is cost visibility per route and, uh, how it maps to token usage. We have a ton of routes — support chat, summary pipeline, internal search.
[00:33] Sophie Grant: Perfect, that's exactly the use case the per-route view was built for. I'll share screen now. (brief pause) Can you see my screen?
[00:42] Priya Shah: Yep.
[00:45] Marco Diaz: Alright, top-left, this is the Usage Overview. Time range up here — you can toggle 1h/24h/7d/30d. The main heatmap shows token consumption by route, and the timeline breaks down input vs output tokens.
[01:03] Priya Shah: Quick question — is that pre- or post-truncation counts? I.e., do you count tokens that were trimmed by our prompt layer?
[01:11] Marco Diaz: Good Q. This reflects tokens actually sent to the model. If you have a pre-filter that trims, those won't show. We also show the raw request and the model request in the trace view.
[01:21] Marta Alvarez: On cost, how granular can we get for chargeback? We need monthly reports by product line.
[01:27] Sophie Grant: You can export per-route cost buckets. The Console maps tokens to dollar estimates using model and infra profile. You can slice by route, model variant, and time window and export CSV.
[01:38] Daniel Kim: Does it handle different model variants automatically? We sometimes fall back from an Llama-large to an optimized ~7B variant.
[01:45] Marco Diaz: Yes, the routing metadata is captured per request. In the per-route dashboard you'll see the model variant, quantization profile, latency percentiles, and cost per 1k tokens.
[01:57] Sophie Grant: Here's a sample per-route dashboard — support-chat route. The top shows throughput (rps), p50/p95 latency, and then token and cost breakdown. See the stacked bar — input vs output tokens.
[02:12] Priya Shah: I see an annotation here that says "KV cache hit" — can you explain? We use a lot of convo history caching.
[02:19] Marco Diaz: Sure — our runtime exposes prefix/KV cache stats. The dashboard shows cache hit rate per route and the estimated savings in tokens. For example, a 60% KV hit rate reduced model token spend by 40% in that window.
[02:34] Daniel Kim: Nice. On billing, can you show us an example where we run a cost simulation?
[02:38] Sophie Grant: Yep — cost estimator. You can plug in expected routes, percent of requests hitting cache, batching settings, and the estimator projects model cost and infra cost. Let's change cache hit to 30% and batching to 0.5s batch wait.
[02:53] Priya Shah: Wait, what's the default batching policy? Our latency SLO for support-chat is 300ms p95.
[02:59] Marco Diaz: We have per-route batching controls. Default is low-latency: batch window 20-50ms. For throughput routes you can increase to 100-500ms. The estimator accounts for latency SLOs and will flag when batching violates your p95 target in simulation.
[03:15] Marta Alvarez: How do you model infra cost versus model token cost? Like, if we use dedicated GPUs vs hosted?
[03:22] Sophie Grant: Two lines — model token cost (licensed + per-token inference cost) and infra cost (GPU hours, efficiency gains from quantization). In Dedicated we also show reserved vs burst cost. You can compare in the estimator.
[03:34] Daniel Kim: Any gotchas on quantization and quality? We have concerns that 4-bit will drop hallucinations but also maybe affect subtle summarization nuance.
[03:44] Marco Diaz: Totally valid. We surface quality regressions in Optimize — you can bind a prompt set and run A/B across quantization levels. We also show sample diffs and a simple scoring metric (ROUGE/BLEU/semantic-sim) to help you gauge tradeoffs.
[03:58] Priya Shah: Good. Security question: our legal team needs SOC 2 and KMS usage. How do you show logs and key management?
[04:06] Sophie Grant: We integrate with customer KMS for private deployments; for hosted we provide managed KMS with BYOK options. Audit logs are available in the Console, retention configurable as an add-on. We'll send the SOC 2 deck after the call.
[04:17] Marta Alvarez: And SSO? We use Okta.
[04:20] Marco Diaz: SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning is supported. Role-based access control is per-route.
[04:27] Priya Shah: Back to the dashboard — can we set alerts on cost anomalies? We had a spike last month from a runaway job.
[04:33] Sophie Grant: Yes — Alerts > Cost anomalies. You can set thresholds (absolute or percent) and webhook to PagerDuty or Slack. Also anomaly detection can auto-flag unusual per-route token spikes.
[04:45] Daniel Kim: Are traces exportable to our X-Ray/Zipkin?
[04:48] Marco Diaz: We export traces via OpenTelemetry — you can push to your tracing backend.
[04:52] Priya Shah: What about per-token breakdown for prompt engineering? We want to know which parts of the prompt are expensive.
[04:58] Marco Diaz: In the trace detail each tokenized chunk is shown; we map cost to prompt sections in the Trace view. It's not perfect (tokenization boundaries can be noisy) but it's good for identifying expensive prefixes.
[05:12] Sophie Grant: Ok, demo pivot — here's a cost-mapping example across three routes: search, support-chat, summaries. You can see search consumes 55% of tokens but support-chat is the biggest infra latency driver due to low batching.
[05:27] Marta Alvarez: If we wanted to do internal chargeback monthly, can you automate label mapping to our product codes?
[05:32] Sophie Grant: Yep — route tags + account mappings. You can tag routes in the Console and those tags map to cost center reports. Exports include the tags.
[05:40] Daniel Kim: For the pilot, what would you recommend? We have 3 high-traffic routes; we'd like to evaluate Dedicated for one and Hosted for the others.
[05:48] Marco Diaz: Typical approach: pick one production-critical route for a dedicated testing lane (reserved capacity) and run a 2-week benchmark capturing p95 latency, cost per token, and error rates. The Console will ingest telemetry and produce the per-route report for you.
[06:02] Priya Shah: How do we set SLOs and break down by route?
[06:06] Marco Diaz: In the Rollouts tab you can set route SLOs and associate fallback policies. If p95 > threshold we can route to a cheaper variant or raise capacity automatically.
[06:17] Sophie Grant: Quick aside — a customer in finance used automated fallback during end-of-day spikes; latency stayed within acceptable bounds and cost went up by a modest percent but uptime was preserved.
[06:29] Priya Shah: Anything else on the Console we should care about?
[06:31] Sophie Grant: There's a Query Insights feature that clusters similar requests; it's helpful for identifying top prompt templates and tuning them. Also an API to pull all metrics if you want to build your own dashboards.
[06:45] Marta Alvarez: Ok, on pricing — can you show an example?
[06:48] Sophie Grant: I'll open a mock pricing export. This is a sample from a comparable customer with similar traffic: shows per-token cost, infra cost, and savings from cache and batching. In this sample, enabling prefix cache and a modest batching policy saved ~32% on token spend.
[07:03] Priya Shah: Do you break out embed costs vs generation? We do embeddings for search indexing and generation for chat.
[07:08] Marco Diaz: Yes — embeds are a separate metric. The Console shows embeddings usage and cost, and you can allocate to product lines separately.
[07:16] Daniel Kim: For dedicated, how many GPUs per pool and what instance types?
[07:20] Sophie Grant: We typically provision A100-ish or H100 depending on model; pool size depends on concurrency, we'll recommend based on your pilot. There's a recommended baseline and a burst policy.
[07:31] Priya Shah: Are model updates versioned? We worry about regressions during rollout.
[07:34] Marco Diaz: Yes — model and config versioning is first-class. Rollouts tab supports canary and A/B with automatic metrics comparison. You can tie evaluations to prompts sets so you can catch regressions.
[07:46] Sophie Grant: Alright, quick demo of creating a per-route dashboard: choose route, add widgets — latency, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit, model variant distribution, and alert rules. Once saved you can pin to a team dashboard.
[08:05] Daniel Kim: Can we programmatically create these via API?
[08:08] Marco Diaz: Yup, Console APIs allow dashboard and alert creation; infra teams like yours typically script this in CI.
[08:14] Priya Shah: Okay — a couple of nitty gritty items: can you capture PII filters before sending to Redwood hosted models? We need to redact PHI.
[08:23] Sophie Grant: For Hosted we have built-in redaction options and you can also run classification hooks pre-send. For Private deployment you keep all data in your VPC so that's often the recommended route for PHI.
[08:36] Marta Alvarez: Finance again — what's the billing cadence and do you support consolidated billing across subsidiaries?
[08:42] Sophie Grant: Monthly billing with cost center tags; consolidated billing is supported and we can generate separate invoices per legal entity.
[08:50] Daniel Kim: Any limitations on retention for traces/metrics?
[08:53] Marco Diaz: Default retention is 90 days for detailed traces, metrics are kept for 13 months; extended retention is available as an add-on.
[09:02] Priya Shah: Sounds good. Could you run through a quick benchmark template so we know what logs and artifacts we need to produce?
[09:09] Marco Diaz: Sure — we'll capture: sample traffic (rps distribution), route definitions, tokenized prompts, expected p95 latency SLOs, and a validation prompt set for quality checks. We recommend running 72-hour baseline then 2-week pilot.
[09:25] Sophie Grant: And we'll provide a benchmarking spreadsheet plus an ingestion guide.
[09:29] Priya Shah: Perfect. Any blockers on our side? We need to get legal's buy-in for Hosted vs Private and Marta needs the budget window.
[09:37] Marta Alvarez: We'll aim to have an internal decision by 2026-06-24.
[09:41] Sophie Grant: Great. Quick recap and next steps: we'll send Pricing + SOC2 + KMS docs, Marco will draft the benchmark plan, Priya will export route usage. Then follow-up next week.
[09:53] Priya Shah: Sounds good, thanks both.
[09:56] Sophie Grant: Thanks everyone — talk soon.
[46:00] End of recording

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "kay vee cache" for KV cache, "vee pee see" for VPC) and speaker adjudication may be imperfect. Links referenced in call: https://redwood.ai/docs/console-dashboard (demo link), https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf (SOC2 deck)
